name: Verb meanings 170
description: A focused inventory of verb meanings for comparing actions and events.
attribution: List, Johann Mattis & Tjuka, Annika & Blum, Frederic & Kučerová, Alžběta & Ugarte, Carlos Barrientos & Rzymski, Christoph & Greenhill, Simon & Forkel, Robert (eds.) 2025. Concepticon v3.4.0. A Resource for the Linking of Concept Lists. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. https://concepticon.clld.org

concepts.definition: To place something over or upon to conceal or protect.
To make full.
To put a large quantity of things onto something.
To establish connection between two or more things.
To cause a liquid to flow into a container.
To set or place an object somewhere.
To cause (an object) to move rapidly through the air, with the force of the hand or arm.
To transport toward somewhere; to take something or somebody with oneself somewhere.
To lift and bring to somewhere else; to transport by lifting.
To make something (an object, a message) go from one place to another.
To transfer the possession or holding (of an object) to another person.
To have somebody see something.
To take possession of property belonging to another without the consent of this owner; most typically when not observed, rather than by force.
To put oneself in a place where one cannot be found, or an object so that the object is hidden.
To pull at something in such a way that it ends up divided.
To move an object or utensil over a surface or other object while maintaining contact, in order that a substance be removed from its surface.
To perform an incision (for example, with a knife).
To be in physical contact with.
To hit against with a sharp blow or to impel, usually with a hand or weapon or to be forcefully or suddenly contacting, e.g. a tree falling down and hitting the ground.
To strike or pound repeatedly, usually in some sort of rhythm.
To put to death; to end a life.
To divide or be divided into pieces and thereby damaged.
To give a name or designation of a common noun that, e.g., reflects a quality.
To utter specific words or notions.
To talk about a story giving its details; to give a detailed account of.
To ask for a service or physical goods, often without returning the favor in kind.
To converse with one or more persons.
To have met and recognize somebody or to be certain or sure about something.
To recall from memory.
To perceive [images] with the eye, without necessarily paying attention to them.
To actively use one's eyes.
To make someone afraid or anxious.
To be scared of; to have an uncontrollable emotion of anxiety about something that causes a scared reaction or frightening impression.
To enjoy, be in favor/favour of.
To chase down prey and (usually) kill it.
To encounter a person, either intentionally or by chance.
To go or come after (in physical space) someone or something.
To give assistance or aid to.
To consume something solid or semi-solid (usually food) by putting it into the mouth and eventually swallowing it.
To remove dirt and grime from an object, using water (usually with soap).
To force air from the lungs out the mouth, sometimes involuntarily, accompanied by a rough sound.
To mount to a high or little accessible place using feet and hands, e.g. a tree, a mountain or a ladder.
To move into a position where the upper body is upright and the bottom is resting  on a surface or the floor.
To move quickly by alternately making a short jump off of either foot.
To propel oneself rapidly upward such that momentum causes the body to become airborne.
To move toward or to reach either the speaker, the person spoken to, or the subject of the speaker's narrative.
To produce harmonious sounds with one's voice.
To live; to reside; to remain or continue.
To become known or apparent.
To cease to live.
To descend in free fall due to the effect of gravity.
The subjective feeling of a decreased body temperature.
To be in need of food.
To fall from the clouds in drops of water.
To get or obtain an item; to come into the possession of something.
To shed tears due to the impact of an emotion.
To create something by combining or assembling materials or parts or by changing it.
Use ones mental power to form ideas or having used ones mental power to form ideas of conviction or belief.
To try to find something.
To squeeze someone in one's arms.
To feel pain.
Feeling mentally uncomfortable because something is missing or wrong.
Whose health is altered.
(Almost) free from liquid or moisture.

To express pleasure, mirth or derision by peculiar movement of the muscles of the face, particularly of the mouth, causing a lighting up of the face and eyes, and usually accompanied by the emission of explosive or chuckling sounds from the chest and throat.
To be consumed by fire.
To make a quick wink of one or both eyelids, often repeatedly.
A person who hunts game.
To grasp with the hands.
To move earth, rocks, etc. out of the way, usually to create a hole.
To remove the skin from food or vegetables.
To break something into small pieces by pressing it flat, or grinding it to powder.
To cut the hair close to the skin with a razor.
To apply a force to (an object), in order that it moves away from the origin of the force that was applied.
To get from one place to another by any means.
To tip laterally.
To pass on knowledge and skills.

To give a loud cry out of pain, fear or excitement. The vocalisation resulted from screaming is distinct from that produced by shrieking in that it is typically characterized by a longer duration and lower pitch.
To prepare a meal or a single dish.
To perceive sound with the ear, without necessarily paying attention to it.
To want to do something or to wish for something to happen.
To go down in water, mud, quicksand etc. or to cause something to go down in it.
To boil some liquid or to be boiling (of some liquid).
To perceive the presence of molecules in the air by inhaling them through the nose.
To clothe oneself; to put on clothes.
To form by combining materials or parts.
To be in a position with the upper body upright and the legs resting.
To move away from a place, a situation or a talk.
To act in a manner such that one has fun; to engage in playful activities expressly for the purpose of recreation.
To move (a door, a window, etc.) so that it closes its opening.
To cause something to be no longer dirty.
To not do what is being asked.
To communicate by the use of words.
Having a low temperature.
Shine with flickering light.
Trying to achieve, to catch, or to reach something or someone.
To enter marriage; to take a husband or a wife.
To look at and interpret letters or other information that is written.
To ask (a question) to somebody; to seek an answer to.
To perform an action.
To cross something (a river, a street etc.).
To release an offspring from one's own body; to cause to be born.
To go into.
To cease working, moving or thinking for some time in order to relieve fatigue.
To consume a liquid through the mouth.
Feeling tired and willing to go to sleep.
To experience while sleeping.
To step awkwardly or to catch your foot on something and almost fall.
To move toward or to reach either the speaker, the person spoken to, or the subject of the speaker's narrative.
To get or obtain an item; to come into the possession of something.
To ask (a question) to somebody; to seek an answer to.
To be suffocated in water or other fluid; to perish by suffocation in water.
To acquire, or attempt to acquire knowledge or an ability to do something.
To address or summon someone.
To continue to be in the same place or state.
To make a quick wink of one or both eyelids, often repeatedly.
To have a very strong desire for something.
Force to go away.
To cause to undergo fire combustion.
To lose moisture, usually through evaporation or absorption.
To bring down by cutting.
To let something fall down.
To bring some liquid into a state of boiling.
To feel joyful; be delighted.
Imposing pain on somebody else.
Emitting or reflecting light readily or in large amounts. [WN:679]
To perceive with the ear (paying attention to what is heard).
To start a fire or light a flame.
Be in an angry state.
Feeling shame or guilt.
To make the inside something accessible by moving an obstacle aside (e.g. a door or covering), or to move said obstacle.
To wish that a past event had not happened.
